alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism despite levothyroxine
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low Free T4, indicating persistent hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting the thyroid tablet, which is the likely primary cause of poor control. Symptoms including tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes are all consistent with hypothyroidism. These overlap with DTG-related weight gain but are better explained by undertreated hypothyroidism. The weight gain (9 kg over a year) may be substantially driven by uncontrolled hypothyroidism rather than DTG alone. Switching DTG for weight gain without first correcting thyroid function may not address the root cause.

evidence.recommended_action: Address levothyroxine adherence and up-titrate dose to achieve TSH target before attributing weight gain to DTG. Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks.

alerts.title: DTG weight gain vs hypothyroidism attribution
alerts.message: Guidelines list abnormal weight gain as a recognised DTG side effect. Patient gained 9 kg in one year with BMI now 33. However, uncontrolled hypothyroidism (TSH 12.4, low Free T4) is an equally plausible cause of weight gain, and the clinician's plan to switch DTG does not address this. Evidence for DTG attribution: weight gain temporally follows DTG use and guidelines recognise it. Evidence against: hypothyroidism is untreated/poorly controlled, and symptoms (cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, puffiness, delayed reflexes) point to thyroid dysfunction. Correcting hypothyroidism first is essential before concluding DTG is the cause.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise hypothyroidism treatment first; reassess weight after TSH normalises before deciding to switch DTG.

alerts.title: Dyslipidaemia and hyperglycaemia risk with DTG and obesity
alerts.message: Guidelines require assessing hyperglycaemia risk before DTG use, with BMI ≥25 as a risk factor. Patient has BMI 33 and multiple hyperglycaemia risk factors (age ≥30, obesity). Fasting glucose is 5.6 mmol/L, below the high-glucose threshold (>6.95 mmol/L fasting) that would contraindicate DTG. However, LDL 4.2 and total cholesterol 6.4 mmol/L indicate dyslipidaemia, compounding cardiovascular risk with obesity. Guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after DTG transition. No 3-monthly glucose monitoring is evident in the plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor fasting glucose every 3 months for the first year per DTG guidelines. Address dyslipidaemia with lifestyle measures and consider lipid-lowering therapy.
